expectations.text: The firmware computes spin direction as a sensor axis plus sign (e.g. from integrated gyro rotation and/or cross products of consecutive samples) and sends it in the BLE packet
expectations.evidence: signed rate along learned spin axis sent over BLE

expectations.text: The firmware handles both twisting around the device's own axis and circular wrist motion where the gyro vector rotates
expectations.evidence: Projects gyro onto a learned axis: handles twist only; circular wrist motion where the gyro vector rotates is not handled

expectations.text: The firmware reports when the direction is unknown/ambiguous (e.g. a confidence flag or threshold) rather than always guessing
The game learns which axis+sign means clockwise for this device and grip through a calibration step where the player spins in a known direction
The calibration result is stored per device (e.g. localStorage keyed by device name) so it is not repeated every session
expectations.evidence: single global localStorage key spinDir.calibration.v1, not per device

expectations.text: The JS maps incoming direction to +1/-1/0 and the mini-game uses it to push the marker right/left
expectations.evidence: read() returns -1/0/1 and push; tug-minigame uses it

expectations.text: The solution includes keyboard keys for spinning clockwise and counter-clockwise so the mini-game can be tested without the stick
expectations.evidence: no keyboard keys for CW/CCW testing
